tools.name: migration_readiness
tools.description: Return migration readiness details for a PLC.

tools.name: migration_readiness_all
tools.description: Return compact migration readiness summaries for all indexed PLCs.

tools.name: tag_diff
tools.description:
Compare tag databases between two PLCs, or track changes via snapshots.

    If compare_to is another PLC ID: side-by-side comparison of all tags.
    Useful for migration verification (does the new CLX have all the PLC-5 tags?).

    If compare_to is None: compare current state against the last saved snapshot.
    First call creates the snapshot and returns a message. Subsequent calls show diffs.
    Each call updates the snapshot to the current state.

    Args:
        plc_id: primary PLC identifier
        compare_to: other PLC ID for cross-PLC mode, or None for snapshot mode

    Returns dict with mode, plc_a, plc_b, tags_only_in_a, tags_only_in_b,
    tags_in_both, description_changes, type_changes, and summary counts.

tools.name: migration_gap_analysis
tools.description:
Analyze what is required to migrate a PLC to ControlLogix.

    If target_plc_id is provided, cross-compares source and target to find
    what has been migrated and what is still missing.

    If target_plc_id is None, analyzes the source PLC alone and produces
    a migration requirements list with an estimated effort rating.

    Args:
        source_plc_id: the PLC being migrated (e.g. 'CH880001')
        target_plc_id: optional ControlLogix migration target PLC ID

    Returns a dict with: source info, I/O mapping, complexity metrics,
    communication links, PlantPAx equivalents needed, description quality,
    HMI impact, estimated effort, and optional target tag mapping.

tools.name: tag_where_used
tools.description:
Return every routine/rung where a tag is used within a single PLC.

    tag_name supports SQL LIKE wildcards (use % not *).
    Array members (e.g. MyTag[0], MyTag[1]) are automatically included —
    pass the base name without wildcards and both the base tag and all
    indexed members are returned.
    For UDT sub-members, append a dot wildcard: tag_name="MyTag.%"

    Returns a list of dicts with keys:
        routine, program, rung_number, usage_type, instruction
    Returns [] if tag_name is empty or not found.

tools.name: tag_find_plant_wide
tools.description:
Search for tags across all PLCs.

    tag_pattern uses * as the wildcard character (converted to % for SQL LIKE).
    Results are limited to 500 rows.

    Returns a list of dicts with keys:
        plc_id, name, data_type, scope, description

    If the result set exceeds 500 rows, a trailing dict
    {"truncated": true, "total_hint": N} is appended.

tools.name: tag_search
tools.description:
Fuzzy/multi-word tag search using FTS5 trigram index.

    Searches both tag names and descriptions. All words in the query must
    match (AND logic). Words shorter than 3 characters are ignored.

    Args:
        query:  One or more search terms, e.g. "conveyor motor" or "emergency stop"
        plc_id: Optional PLC filter, e.g. "CH530001"
        limit:  Maximum results to return (default 50)

    Returns a dict with keys:
        query, result_count, truncated, results

    Each result has: plc_id, name, data_type, scope, description, tag_type

tools.name: tag_context
tools.description:
Return a unified 360° view of a single tag within a PLC.

    Combines tag definition, all read/write references, producer/consumer
    links, MSG links, and AOI instance usages into one response.

    Args:
        plc_id:   The PLC to search (e.g. 'CH530001').
        tag_name: Exact tag name (no wildcards).

    Returns a dict with keys: definition, reads, writes, produced_consumed,
    msg_links, aoi_instances, summary.
    If the tag is not found, returns {"error": "tag not found", ...}.

tools.name: tag_annotate
tools.description:
Update a tag's description and/or confidence level.

    Use this to correct wrong descriptions, verify good ones, or flag suspects.

    Args:
        plc_id:               PLC to update (e.g. 'CH530001').
        tag_name:             Exact tag name.
        new_description:      New description text (optional).
        confidence:           New confidence tier (optional). One of:
                              imported_unverified, imported_likely, verified,
                              suspected_wrong, no_description.
        verified_by:          Name of person verifying (optional).
        verified_at:          ISO 8601 timestamp of verification (optional).
                              Defaults to current UTC time when confidence='verified'.
        verification_method:  Short description of the workflow used, e.g.
                              "tag_suspect_descriptions sweep + rung citation".
        coverage_notes:       Free-text field for known limitations at verification
                              time, e.g. "B3 not imported in symbol export".

    Returns the updated tag record as a dict, or an error dict.

tools.name: verification_summary
tools.description:
List PLCs that have at least one verified tag, with verification metadata.

    Returns one row per PLC showing the earliest verification date, verifier,
    method, coverage notes, and counts of verified vs total active tags.

    Args:
        plc_id: Optional PLC filter. If omitted, returns all PLCs with verified tags.

    Returns a list of dicts, each with:
        plc_id, verified_tag_count, total_tag_count, earliest_verified_at,
        verified_by (most common), verification_method (most common),
        coverage_notes (concatenated, distinct).

tools.name: backfill_symbol_file_sources
tools.description:
Backfill description_sources table from existing symbol-file tag descriptions.

    Populates the multi-source reconciliation layer with symbol_file entries
    (base_confidence=0.2) drawn from tags with source='symbol_import'.
    Tags with NULL or empty descriptions are skipped.

    Idempotent — safe to call multiple times.  Does NOT modify the tags table.

    Args:
        plc_id: Optional PLC filter (e.g. 'CH550003').  None processes all PLCs.

    Returns dict with: plc_id_filter, rows_examined, rows_inserted,
    rows_skipped_existing.

tools.name: backfill_engineer_verified_sources
tools.description:
Backfill description_sources table from engineer-verified tag descriptions.

    Populates the multi-source reconciliation layer with engineer_verified
    entries (base_confidence=0.9) drawn from tags with
    description_confidence='verified'.  Preserves original verified_by and
    verified_at provenance.

    Idempotent — safe to call multiple times.  Does NOT modify the tags table.

    Args:
        plc_id: Optional PLC filter (e.g. 'CH550003').  None processes all PLCs.

    Returns dict with: plc_id_filter, rows_examined, rows_inserted,
    rows_skipped_existing.

tools.name: reconcile_descriptions
tools.description:
Consolidate multi-source tag descriptions into a unified reconciliation view.

    For each tag in plc_id with at least one description_sources entry, returns
    the winning description (highest base_confidence source), all contributing
    sources, and a disagreement flag when two sources have conflicting text.

    Disagreement detection uses normalized comparison (lowercase, collapsed
    whitespace, trailing punctuation stripped).  Phrasing variance and scope
    variance are not flagged — only exact normalized mismatches.

    Tags with no description_sources entries are not included (they remain in
    tags.description-only mode and are unaffected by this tool).

    Does NOT modify any table.

    Args:
        plc_id:    PLC to reconcile (e.g. 'CH550003').
        tag_name:  Optional single tag to reconcile.  None returns all tags
                   in plc_id with description_sources entries.

    Returns a single reconciliation dict (tag_name given) or list of dicts
    (tag_name omitted).  Each dict has: plc_id, tag_name,
    consolidated_description, consolidated_source, consolidated_confidence,
    source_count, all_sources, disagreement_flag, disagreement_details.

tools.name: tag_suspect_descriptions
tools.description:
Find tags where descriptions may be unreliable.

    Returns plant tags (not library) with suspect confidence tiers.
    Useful for auditing tag descriptions that need human review.

    Args:
        plc_id:            Optional PLC filter (e.g. 'CH730001').
        confidence_filter: Optional filter to a single tier
                           (e.g. 'imported_unverified', 'no_description', 'suspected_wrong').

    Returns a list of dicts with: plc_id, tag_name, description,
    description_confidence, description_source, programs_used (list of str).
    Sorted: suspected_wrong first, then imported_unverified, then no_description.
    Limited to 100 results.

tools.name: tag_screen_usage
tools.description:
Find all HMI screens that display a given PLC tag.

    Args:
        plc_id:   The PLC whose tag to search for.
        tag_name: Tag name or PLC-5 address (supports SQL LIKE wildcards).

    Returns list of dicts: screen_name, screen_plc_id, element_name,
    binding_type, expression.

tools.name: tag_full_chain
tools.description:
Trace a tag from PLC logic through HMI displays — the complete picture.

    Combines:
    1. Tag definition (data type, scope, description, confidence)
    2. PLC rung usage (programs, routines, rung numbers)
    3. HMI screen bindings (which screens display this tag)
    4. Produced/consumed cross-PLC links

    Args:
        plc_id:   PLC to search (e.g. 'CH530001').
        tag_name: Exact tag name or PLC-5 address.

    Returns a dict with keys: definition, plc_usage, hmi_bindings,
    produced_consumed, summary.

tools.name: find_orphan_tags
tools.description:
Tags on a PLC with no description, no vault note, and no rung comment — a documentation queue.

    Returns a list of dicts with keys:
        tag_name, data_type, description_confidence, usage_count
    Ordered by usage_count descending.

tools.name: rung_search
tools.description:
Full-text search across rung content and comments using SQL LIKE.

    Address normalization: if the query looks like a PLC-5 B-file or N-file
    address, it is automatically expanded to match both the shorthand form
    (B13/913, N7/1609) and the canonical word:bit form (B13:57/1, N7:100/9).
    This is transparent to the caller — either form finds rungs regardless
    of which form was written in the original PC5 source file.

    Args:
        query:            Search string. Accepts SQL LIKE wildcards (%), plain
                          text substring, or any PLC-5/CLX address in either
                          shorthand (B13/913) or canonical (B13:57/1) notation.
        plc_id:           Restrict to one PLC (None = all PLCs).
        include_disabled: Include disabled rungs (default False).

    Returns up to 200 results. If truncated, the last entry has
    {"truncated": true}. Each result has:
        plc_id, program, routine, rung_number, content_snippet,
        comment_snippet, disabled

tools.name: rung_forensic
tools.description:
Raw rung extraction for forensic analysis. No classification, no interpretation.

    Exactly one of rung_numbers, addresses, or output_targets must be provided.

    Mode 1 (rung_numbers): extract specific rungs by number.
    Mode 2 (addresses): find all rungs referencing the given addresses, then extract.
      Mode 2 also produces a per-address usage inventory (XIC/XIO/write counts).
    Mode 3 (output_targets): find all rungs that WRITE to the given addresses.
      Queries address_xref with usage_type='write'. Returns one rung per unique
      write rung (address_xref may have multiple rows per rung for the same address).
      Each rung record includes a writes_to field listing which targets it matched.
      Emits warnings for targets with no write references (possible dead outputs).
      Mode 4 (intent-based descriptor search): deferred.

    Args:
        plc_id:               PLC identifier (e.g. 'CH550003')
        rung_numbers:         Mode 1 — list of rung numbers (int) to extract
        addresses:            Mode 2 — list of PLC-5/CLX address strings (read OR write)
        output_targets:       Mode 3 — list of address strings to anchor on write references
        include_tag_records:  Pull tags table record for every address in extracted rungs
        include_rung_comments: Include rung comment field in output
        output_file:          If set, write Markdown to this path
        overwrite:            Allow overwriting output_file if it already exists
        render_mode:          Optional render mode for each rung — '' (off), 'boolean',
                              'indented', or 'annotated'.  When set, each rung record
                              includes rendered_content in the Markdown output.

    Returns dict with:
        document:      Markdown string
        mode:          1, 2, or 3
        rung_count:    number of rungs extracted (not_found excluded)
        address_count: unique addresses referenced across all rungs
        tag_hits:      addresses found in tags table
        tag_misses:    addresses not in tags table
        warnings:      list[str] — Mode 3 warnings (dead outputs, etc.)

tools.name: render_rung
tools.description:
Render a PLC rung as structured text.

    Modes:
    - 'boolean':   one AND/OR expression per output — best for analysis and reverse engineering
    - 'indented':  tree-indented with branch markers — best for visual understanding
    - 'annotated': indented with tag descriptions inline — best for documentation

    Args:
        plc_id:      PLC identifier (e.g. 'CH510002')
        rung_number: Rung number to render
        routine:     Optional routine name to disambiguate when the same rung number
                     appears in multiple routines.  Leave blank to use the first match.
        mode:        One of 'boolean', 'indented', 'annotated'

    Returns:
        JSON string with keys: plc_id, rung_number, routine, program, mode, rendered,
        outputs (list of {address, type, expression, description}), raw_content, comment.

tools.name: routine_call_tree
tools.description:
Walk the JSR call graph from a starting routine and return the call tree.

    Args:
        plc_id:        The PLC to search.
        routine_name:  Starting routine name (e.g. 'MainRoutine').
        max_depth:     Maximum recursion depth (default 5).

    Returns a dict with keys: root, plc_id, tree, stats.
    stats includes: total_routines, max_depth_reached, cycles_detected.

tools.name: get_plc5_instruction_reference
tools.description:
Return the semantic definition, operands, timing, patterns, and gotchas
    for a PLC-5 / RSLogix 5 instruction.

    Call this when analyzing PLC-5 ladder logic and you need to understand
    what an instruction does, how its operands work, or what timing behavior
    to expect.

    Args:
        mnemonic: Instruction name (e.g., 'TON', 'JSR', 'PID', 'BST').

tools.name: get_rung_pattern
tools.description:
Return a validated rung pattern template with a real plant example.

    Use this to understand common PLC logic patterns or to construct new
    rungs based on proven templates.

    Args:
        pattern_name: Pattern key (e.g., 'timer_on_delay_basic',
                      'branch_setpoint_selector', 'clx_plantpax_motor_config').

tools.name: search_rung_patterns
tools.description:
Search the rung pattern library by natural language description.

    Use this when you know what you want a rung to DO but don't know
    the pattern name.

    Args:
        query: Natural language (e.g., 'select between two setpoints',
               'clamp PID output', 'detect rising edge').

tools.name: generate_ascii_rung
tools.description:
Generate a complete, ready-to-paste ASCII rung by filling a pattern
    template with specific addresses.

    CRITICAL: Before calling this, verify all addresses against NEXUS using
    tag_find_plant_wide to ensure no conflicts.

    Args:
        pattern_name: Pattern to use (e.g., 'timer_on_delay_basic').
        substitutions: Placeholder replacements, e.g.:
            {'condition': 'XIC B3/17', 'n': '50', 'timebase': '1.0',
             'preset': '300'}

tools.name: add_rung_pattern
tools.description:
Add a new validated rung pattern to the library for future reuse.

    Call this when you encounter a rung worth preserving as a reusable
    template during plant analysis work. Persists to
    ~/.nexus/custom_patterns.json.

    Args:
        pattern_name: Unique key (e.g., 'analog_scaling_with_clamp').
        intent: What the pattern does in plain English.
        platform: 'PLC-5' or 'ControlLogix'.
        ascii_template: Template with {placeholder} substitutions.
        parameters: Dict describing each placeholder.
        plant_source: Where this was found (e.g., 'CH880001 Rung 115').
        plant_ascii: The actual rung content from the plant.
        notes: Engineering notes.

tools.name: semantic_rung_search
tools.description:
Natural-language semantic search over PLC ladder rungs using local embeddings.

    Finds rungs by meaning, not exact tag match — e.g.
    'where is the main conveyor interlock unlatched' surfaces OTU/interlock rungs
    ranked by semantic similarity to the query.

    Requires ``nexus patterns embed`` to have been run for the target PLC, and
    the optional dependencies to be installed:
        pip install sentence-transformers sqlite-vec

    Args:
        query:   Natural-language description of the logic you are looking for.
        plc_id:  Optional PLC filter (e.g. 'Dryer_PLC', 'CH550003').
                 When omitted, all indexed PLCs are searched.
        limit:   Maximum results to return (capped at 50; default 20).

    Returns a dict with:
        - results: list of {rung_id, plc_id, routine, rung_number,
                             content_snippet, score}
          ordered by ascending distance (most similar first).
        - count: number of results returned.
        - query: the original query string.
        - plc_id: the filter applied (None = all PLCs).
        - available: False (with a note) when deps are missing or vec tables
          have not been populated.

tools.name: ingest_factorytalk_csv
tools.description: Ingest a FactoryTalk View ME CSV tag database export into HMI tables.

tools.name: ingest_quickdesigner_bindings
tools.description: Ingest QuickDesigner JSON bindings into hmi_projects + hmi_tag_bindings.

tools.name: hmi_search_by_address
tools.description: Find every HMI binding across all projects referencing a given PLC address.

tools.name: ftview_rung_xref
tools.description:
Given a PLC tag address, return both HMI bindings and PLC ladder rungs.

    Combines hmi_search_by_address with a rung content search to answer:
    'Where is this tag displayed on the HMI, and what PLC logic controls it?'
    Most useful when tracing a tag from operator screen through to controller.

    Args:
        plc_address: PLC address to cross-reference (e.g. 'PD10:14.PV', 'N7:124')
        plc_id: Optional PLC scope (e.g. 'CH530001')

tools.name: hmi_coverage_by_plc
tools.description: What percentage of a PLC's tags are displayed on at least one HMI?

tools.name: hmi_project_summary
tools.description: Summary of one or all HMI projects with live binding counts.

tools.name: ingest_ftview_displays
tools.description:
Ingest FT View ME display XML files into NEXUS HMI object catalog.
    display_paths_json is a JSON array of absolute file paths to display XML files.

tools.name: ingest_ftview_project_folder
tools.description: Walk project_folder for FT View display XML files and ingest all found into NEXUS.

tools.name: ftview_find_objects
tools.description: Find FT View HMI objects by type, screen, or tag reference pattern.

tools.name: ftview_object_example
tools.description:
Get one representative copy-pasteable XML example for a FT View object type.
    Use this instead of reading full display XML files — ~36x token savings.

tools.name: ftview_screen_layout
tools.description: Get all objects on a FT View screen in tree form with nested group children.

tools.name: ftview_tag_pattern
tools.description: Find all FT View HMI objects referencing tags matching a pattern (e.g. 'N7:124' or 'PD10:').

tools.name: ftview_object_catalog
tools.description: Return the full FT View object type catalog with counts, common properties, and example XML.

tools.name: ftview_navigation_graph
tools.description:
Return the screen-to-screen navigation graph for an FTView HMI project.

    Returns an adjacency dict (from_screen → [to_screen, ...]) and a full edge
    list showing which button element triggers each navigation. Useful for
    understanding HMI menu structure and verifying operator access paths.

    Args:
        project_name: HMI project name (e.g. 'CH530001 C11 Curing Oven')
        project_id: Integer project ID (alternative to project_name)

tools.name: ftview_validate
tools.description:
Validate a FactoryTalk View ME display XML file.

    Checks all enabled rules and returns ALL violations at once — no more
    one-error-at-a-time import loops. If fix=True, auto-fixes deterministic
    errors and writes to {filename}_fixed.xml (never overwrites original).
    If use_catalog=True, also compares against the NEXUS object catalog to
    flag deviations from plant-standard patterns.

    Args:
        xml_path: Absolute path to the display XML file.
        fix: If True, run auto-fix and return path to fixed file.
        use_catalog: If True, run catalog comparison (requires NEXUS DB).

    Returns:
        {
            "valid": bool,
            "error_count": int,
            "warning_count": int,
            "errors": [{"rule_id", "severity", "element_tag", "element_name",
                        "line_number", "message", "fix_suggestion", "context"}, ...],
            "warnings": [...],
            "summary": str,
            "fixed_path": str or None   # set when fix=True
        }

tools.name: screen_inventory
tools.description:
List all indexed HMI screens with binding counts.

    Args:
        plc_id: Optional PLC filter.

    Returns list of dicts: plc_id, name, display_number, width, height,
    binding_count, source_type.

tools.name: screen_tag_bindings
tools.description:
Get all tag bindings for a named HMI screen.

    Args:
        display_name: Screen name (e.g. 'ExecWing').
        plc_id: Optional PLC filter if multiple PLCs have same screen name.

    Returns list of dicts: element_name, element_type, shortcut, raw_tag,
    resolved_plc_id, binding_type, expression, connection_name.

tools.name: ignition_tag_search
tools.description:
Search indexed Ignition tags by name, path, or PLC tag reference.

    Args:
        query:  Search term (SQL LIKE — use % for wildcards).
        device: Optional Ignition device name filter (e.g. 'C11Oven').
        limit:  Maximum results (default 50).

    Returns a dict with keys: query, result_count, results.
    Each result: tag_path, name, tag_type, device_name, plc_tag,
    resolved_plc_id, opc_item_path.

tools.name: ignition_device_map_tool
tools.description:
List all Ignition OPC device-to-PLC mappings with tag counts.

    Returns a dict with keys: device_count, resolved, unresolved, devices.
    Each device: device_name, plc_id, tag_count.

tools.name: ignition_resolve_all
tools.description:
Batch-resolve unresolved Ignition tags against the device map and known PLC IDs.

    Four resolution strategies applied in order:
    1. Seed new device map entries for known unresolved devices
    2. Device map lookup — device_name matches ignition_device_map
    3. CH-number pattern — device_name starts with 'CH' followed by 6 digits
    4. Tag path mining — tag_path contains instrument tags with CH-number prefix
       (e.g. 'CH51PI1901' in path → shop order 51 → forming PLCs)

    Returns counts per strategy and list of still-unresolved devices.

tools.name: ftview_writable_tags_audit
tools.description:
List all HMI elements that can write to PLC tags (safety audit).

    Returns every numericInputEnable, multistateButton, pushButton, and listSelector
    element across all indexed displays, with the PLC address each element writes to.
    Scope to one project (project_name) or one PLC (plc_id).

    Args:
        project_name: Filter to one HMI project
        project_id: Integer project ID (alternative to project_name)
        plc_id: Filter to one PLC's writable tags (e.g. 'CH530001')

tools.name: ftview_state_labels
tools.description:
Return operator-visible state labels for multistate HMI indicators/buttons.

    Given a PLC address (e.g. 'N7:124' or 'Drive1.Status'), returns the caption text
    and color for each integer value displayed on every multistate indicator watching
    that address. Answers: 'what does the operator see when this tag equals 2?'

    Args:
        plc_address: PLC tag address to look up (e.g. 'PD10:14.Status')
        project_id: Scope to one HMI project (0 = all projects)
        object_name: Look up states for a specific named indicator/button

tools.name: nexus_reindex
tools.description:
Trigger a re-index of PLC source files into the NEXUS database.

    Args:
        plc_id:      Limit re-index to a single PLC (None = all PLCs).
        incremental: Skip files whose hash has not changed since last index.

    Returns the report dict produced by IngestPipeline.run().

tools.name: ingest_l5x
tools.description:
Ingest a single ControlLogix L5X export file into NEXUS.

    Args:
        l5x_path: Absolute path to the .L5X file
        plc_id: PLC identifier (e.g. 'CH300001')

tools.name: coverage_gap
tools.description: Measure ladder-logic address coverage against the tags table for a PLC.

tools.name: promote_raw_addresses_to_tags
tools.description:
Promote rung-referenced PLC-5 addresses with no tag entry into synthetic tag rows.

    Closes the ingestion gap between address_xref (populated from rung parsing) and the
    tags table (populated only from the SY6 symbol exporter). Each promoted address gets
    a synthetic tag row with source='raw_address_promotion' and a coverage_notes string
    recording the promotion date.

    Idempotent: safe to call multiple times — running twice produces zero new rows on the
    second call. Does not modify any existing tag row.

    Does NOT auto-run during indexing — call explicitly after indexing a PLC.

    Args:
        plc_id: PLC to promote (e.g. 'CH850001').

    Returns dict with: plc_id, total_xref_canonicals, already_in_tags, promoted, errors.

tools.name: generate_io_inventory
tools.description:
Generate a flat physical I/O inventory for a PLC with trust levels and HMI cross-references.

    Unions tags-table I/O addresses with address_xref I/O canonicals. Classifies each point
    by physical class (DI/AI/DO/AO) and trust level (Verified / Logic-confirmed / Import-only).
    Returns a Markdown document with four sorted tables plus a priority verification list.

    Args:
        plc_id: PLC identifier (e.g., 'CH550003')
        output_path: Optional file path to write the Markdown output. Always returns the string.

    Returns JSON with keys: markdown, output_path, summary {total/di/ai/do/ao/verified/…}, io_points.

tools.name: group_io_by_area
tools.description:
Cluster a PLC's I/O points into functional areas by rack/group prefix and rung co-occurrence.

    Groups addresses by their I:/O: file-number prefix, pairs adjacent I and O groups into
    functional areas, then names each area from the majority description keyword theme.

    Args:
        plc_id: PLC identifier

    Returns JSON with key 'areas': list of {area_name, rationale, prefixes, addresses, dependencies}.

tools.name: find_area_interlocks
tools.description:
Find rungs where addresses from two different I/O areas co-appear.

    Useful for identifying interlock dependencies between functional areas before field verification.

    Args:
        plc_id: PLC identifier
        area_a_addresses: JSON array of canonical addresses for area A (e.g., '["I:014/00","I:014/01"]')
        area_b_addresses: JSON array of canonical addresses for area B

    Returns JSON with shared_rung_count and list of shared_rungs with addresses per area per rung.

tools.name: generate_io_package
tools.description:
Generate a complete I/O documentation package for a PLC (inventory + verification plan).

    Runs the seven-stage pipeline:
      1. Flat physical I/O inventory with trust levels
      2. Area grouping by rack/group prefix
      3. Cross-area interlock detection
      4. Desk review (bulk rung-context analysis, max 50 inferences)
      5. Risk-sort areas (highest unresolved count first)
      6. Render two Markdown documents
      7. Write files to output_dir (defaults to ~/.nexus/reports/{plc_id}/)

    Read-only against the NEXUS database.

    Args:
        plc_id: PLC identifier (e.g., 'CH510002', 'CH550003')
        output_dir: Optional directory to write the two output files. Defaults to ~/.nexus/reports/{plc_id}/

    Returns JSON summary with paths, total_io_points, desk_review_summary, areas, execution_time_seconds.

tools.name: onboard_plc
tools.description:
Run the full PLC analysis pipeline in a single call.

    Stages:
      [1] reindex              — scan source files (skip_reindex=True by default for MCP)
      [2] promote raw addresses — Path A: 100% tag coverage
      [3] classify signal roles — 13-role taxonomy
      [4] coverage gap          — verify coverage %
      [5] I/O package           — inventory + verification plan + desk review
      [6] sister-diff           — compare against sister PLCs (only when sisters given)

    Stages 1–5 are fatal: an exception in any stage stops the remaining stages and
    returns the partial results dict. Stage 4 coverage < 100% is a warning, not a stop.
    Stage 6 is non-fatal: failure is captured in results but does not suppress Stage 5 output.

    Args:
        plc_id:           PLC to analyze (e.g. 'CH550003').
        sisters:          Comma-separated sister PLCs for Stage 6
                          (e.g. 'CH550001,CH550002,CH550004').
        skip_reindex:     Skip Stage 1 — default True (PLC is already indexed in MCP context).
        skip_path_a:      Skip Stage 2 (Path A promotion already run).
        skip_sister_diff: Skip Stage 6 even when sisters are provided.
        output_dir:       Output directory for generated files.
                          Default: ~/.nexus/reports/{plc_id}/
        auto_promote:     Pass --auto-promote to sister_diff_report (Stage 6).

    Returns JSON string with one key per executed stage plus '_total_elapsed'.
    Each stage value is a dict with 'success', 'elapsed', and stage-specific fields.

tools.name: ingest_quickdesigner_descriptions
tools.description:
Ingest HMI label descriptions from a QuickDesigner parser JSON output file.

    Reads a JSON file produced by quickdesigner_parse.py -f json, matches
    each binding's canonical PLC address to the tags table for plc_id, and
    inserts description_sources rows with source_type='hmi_quickdesigner'
    (base_confidence=0.8) for bindings that have an operator-visible label.

    Bindings without label_off text (bit_lamps, numeric displays) are not
    stored — presence without a label doesn't constitute a description.

    Idempotent — bindings already ingested from the same source_file are
    skipped.  Does NOT modify the tags table.

    Args:
        plc_id:              Target PLC (e.g. 'CH550003').
        parser_output_path:  Path to the JSON file from quickdesigner_parse.py.

    Returns dict with: plc_id, source_file, bindings_examined, bindings_matched,
    bindings_with_labels, rows_inserted, rows_skipped_existing, bindings_unmatched.

tools.name: ingest_vision_descriptions
tools.description:
Ingest HMI label descriptions from an Ignition Vision binding extractor output.

    Placeholder: the Vision extractor currently produces Markdown output and
    the primary test PLC (CH340001) is not indexed in NEXUS.  This tool
    validates schema compatibility and returns the expected summary structure
    but inserts 0 rows for current inputs.

    Will be upgraded to full ingestion when JSON output format and PLC indexing
    are available.

    Args:
        plc_id:              Target PLC (e.g. 'CH340001').
        parser_output_path:  Path to the Vision extractor output file.

    Returns dict with: plc_id, source_file, bindings_examined, bindings_matched,
    bindings_with_labels, rows_inserted, rows_skipped_existing, bindings_unmatched, note.

tools.name: extract_rung_comments
tools.description:
Extract rung comments attributed to their write-type output targets (dry run).

    Reads rung comments from indexed PLC data and attributes each comment to
    the address(es) written by that rung.  Does NOT write to description_sources —
    returns the candidate list for inspection before committing to ingestion.

    Join path: rungs → routines → address_xref on (plc_id, routine, rung_number).
    Only write-type outputs are attributed.  Disabled rungs are excluded.

    Filters applied:
    - Trimmed comment length >= 15 characters
    - Comment must not contain maintenance markers (TODO:, XXX:, FIXME:, TBD:,
      N/A, 'left blank', 'not used', 'spare', 'unused')

    Args:
        plc_id: Optional PLC filter (e.g. 'CH550003').  None returns all PLCs.

    Returns dict with: plc_id_filter, rungs_with_comments, rungs_after_filter,
    attributions_produced, skipped_too_short, skipped_maintenance,
    extractions (list of {plc_id, tag_name, description, source_location,
    instruction}).

tools.name: ingest_rung_comments
tools.description:
Ingest rung comments into description_sources as source_type='rung_comment'.

    Extracts rung comments via extract_rung_comments, then inserts each
    attribution as a description_sources row with base_confidence=0.3.

    Idempotency: keyed on (plc_id, tag_name, source_type, source_location).
    A tag referenced as output in multiple commented rungs accumulates multiple
    rung_comment rows — one per rung — each with its own source_location.
    Re-running the same PLC inserts 0 new rows.

    Does NOT modify the tags table or any existing description_sources rows.

    Args:
        plc_id: Optional PLC filter (e.g. 'CH550003').  None processes all PLCs.

    Returns dict with: plc_id_filter, rungs_with_comments, rungs_after_filter,
    attributions_produced, rows_inserted, rows_skipped_existing.

tools.name: plc_impact_analysis
tools.description:
Return the full communication footprint of a PLC.

    Returns a dict with keys:
        plc_id, msg_sources, msg_targets,
        produces_to, consumes_from, unresolved_links

tools.name: aoi_instances_find
tools.description:
Find all instances of a named AOI across the plant (or within one PLC).

    Returns a list of dicts with keys:
        plc_id, program, routine, rung_number, instance_tag

tools.name: aoi_library_search
tools.description:
Search AOI definitions in the Engineering Library.

    Args:
        name_pattern: AOI name pattern (use * as wildcard, e.g. P_Motor or P_*)
        library_name: Optional filter by library name (e.g. PlantPAx)
        version: Optional filter by library version (e.g. v4.10.06)
        plant_standard_only: If True, return only plant standard version AOIs

    Returns:
        dict with keys: query, result_count, truncated, results

tools.name: aoi_version_check
tools.description:
Check AOI versions in plant PLCs against the plant standard library.

    For each AOI instance in live plant programs, compares the embedded AOI
    revision against the plant standard library version.

    Args:
        plc_id: Optional PLC CH number (e.g. CH530001). None checks all plant PLCs.

    Returns:
        dict with checked/current/outdated/not_in_library counts and instances list.

tools.name: plant_summary
tools.description: Return high-level statistics for the entire NEXUS knowledge graph.

tools.name: address_xref
tools.description: Full cross-reference for any PLC address.

tools.name: address_xref_summary
tools.description:
Lightweight address cross-reference — counts and related address lists only.
    Use this for quick checks; use address_xref for full rung-level detail.

    Args:
        plc_id: PLC identifier
        address: Any address format

    Returns dict with counts and related address lists.

tools.name: address_trace_chain
tools.description:
Trace the signal chain through PLC logic for any address.

    Follow an address backward to find its source(s) and/or forward to find
    its destination(s). Recursively traces through MOV, ADD, SUB, etc.

    Args:
        plc_id: PLC identifier (e.g., 'CH880001')
        address: Starting address in any format
        direction: 'backward' (find sources), 'forward' (find destinations), or 'both'
        max_depth: Maximum recursion depth (default 5)

    Returns dict with:
        'address': canonical starting address
        'backward_chain': list of {depth, address, written_in_rung, instruction, source_address}
        'forward_chain': list of {depth, address, read_in_rung, instruction, feeds_into}
        'complete_path': human-readable summary string

tools.name: get_state_machine
tools.description:
Return detected ladder state machines for a PLC, optionally filtered to one routine.

    Output per machine: register, idiom, ordered states with labels, transition
    table (from→to, gate_tag, condition_type, enabled), and per-step action table.
    Counter/sequencer (PLC-5) machines report states+actions only — transitions are
    not MOV-driven and are omitted by design (reported as a gap), not inferred.

    Run `nexus patterns detect --plc <id>` first to populate the detection tables.

    Args:
        plc_id:       PLC identifier (e.g. 'Dryer_PLC', 'CH850001').
        routine_name: Optional routine name to return only machines in that routine.

    Returns a dict with:
        plc_id, machines (list of machine dicts), machine_count.
        Each machine dict: routine_name, register, idiom, state_count,
          transition_count, states (list), transitions (list), actions (list), notes.
        Returns a note dict if no machines are detected.

tools.name: find_first_out_faults
tools.description:
Return detected first-out fault-latch groups for a PLC.

    First-out latches record the FIRST fault in a cascade and block subsequent
    captures until reset.  Each group identifies the captured FO register (the
    tag that holds the first-fault code), the active-flag tag (XIO/OTL self-latch
    that blocks re-capture), the reset path (XIC command that OTUs the flag),
    and the ordered member fault sources (MOV sources writing into the FO register,
    with optional sequence hints).

    Run ``nexus patterns detect --plc <id>`` first to populate the detection tables.

    Args:
        plc_id: PLC identifier (e.g. 'Dryer_PLC').

    Returns a dict with:
        plc_id, groups (list), group_count.
        Each group dict: routine_name, fo_register, active_flag_tag, reset_tag,
          latch_rung, member_count, members (list of {fault_tag, sequence_hint, rung_number}).
        Returns a note explaining the signature when no groups are detected.

tools.name: list_documented_plcs
tools.description: List all PLCs that have been documented via the full pipeline.

tools.name: find_interlocks
tools.description: Trace all interlocks and permissives required for an output to energize.

tools.name: classify_signal_roles
tools.description:
Classify PLC-5 addresses by structural role based on ladder instruction patterns.

    Examines the address_xref table instruction evidence for each canonical
    address and assigns one or more roles from a fixed taxonomy:

    latch, one_shot, output_coil, timer, counter, integer_register,
    control_register, input, output, pid_register, message, status_word,
    unclassified.

    Role assignment is pattern-based (observable instructions), not semantic
    inference.  PLC-5 only — ControlLogix tags are not classified.

    When tag_name is omitted the full PLC is classified and a role-distribution
    summary (the "PLC fingerprint") is returned first.

    Args:
        plc_id:   PLC identifier (e.g. 'CH550001').
        tag_name: Optional canonical address to classify a single tag
                  (e.g. 'B3:5/0').  When omitted, all addresses are classified.

    Returns a dict with:
        - Single-tag: plc_id, canonical, file_type, roles, primary_role,
          evidence, read_count, write_count.
        - Full-PLC: plc_id, summary (role_distribution, total_classified,
          multi_role_count, unclassified_count), classifications (list).

tools.name: ote_conflict_audit
tools.description:
Scan every output coil (OTE/OTL/OTU) write site in the PLC and flag
    addresses with more than one writer.

    Also detects word-level writes (MOV/COP/CPS/FLL/CLR) that target a DINT
    at the word level — these silently overwrite all bit assignments in one scan
    and are the most dangerous form of the OTE conflict pattern.

    Severity levels returned:
        HIGH            Multiple OTE in the same task (last-wins guaranteed).
        HIGH-CROSS-TASK Multiple OTE across different tasks (verify priority).
        MEDIUM          Mix of OTE + OTL/OTU (may be intentional safety latch).
        LOW             Multiple OTL or OTU only (usually safe).
        WORD_LEVEL      MOV/COP/etc to a DINT word (engineer must triage).

    Args:
        plc_id: PLC identifier (e.g. 'NFK-DRYER-01').

    Returns a dict with scan_stats, conflicts (with write_sites and verdict),
    word_level_overwrites, and clean_outputs count.

tools.name: dint_bit_audit
tools.description:
Audit DINT arbitration tags for bit-level write uniqueness.

    Detects the following conditions on each bit of every DINT tag matching
    tag_pattern:
        DUAL_OTE        Two OTE writers on the same bit — Anomaly B class bug.
                        Scan-order conflict within the arbitration layer.
        LATCH_PATTERN   OTL + OTU on same bit — verify intentional with comment.
        MIXED           OTE co-exists with OTL/OTU — suspicious, review needed.
        UNCLOSED_LATCH  OTL with no OTU — bit can never self-clear.
        UNCLOSED_UNLATCH OTU with no OTL — likely dead code.

    Also detects:
        ORPHANED_DINT   Tag exists in tag table but has zero write sites.
        WORD_LEVEL      MOV/COP/etc writing the whole DINT word.

    Runs a pre-flight check to warn if address_level='bit' is not populated
    for any OTE rows (which would cause silent misses in the audit).

    Args:
        plc_id:      PLC identifier (e.g. 'NFK-DRYER-01').
        tag_pattern: SQL LIKE pattern for DINT tag names (default 'Seq_%_Start'
                     covers all arbitration tags on NFK-DRYER-01).

    Returns a dict with warnings, summary, conflicts, orphaned_dint_tags,
    latch_bits_needing_review, and word_level_overwrites.

tools.name: nexus_status
tools.description: NEXUS server health: schema version, PLC count, tag count.

tools.name: generate_sequence_of_operations
tools.description:
Generate a Sequence of Operations document for a PLC.

    Produces plain-English descriptions of how the PLC program
    operates, including: what conditions enable each output,
    timing sequences, PID loop configurations, and interlock chains.

    Args:
        plc_id: PLC identifier (e.g., 'CH880001')
        scope: 'full' (all logic), 'outputs_only' (just output chains),
               'pid' (PID loops only)
        output_format: 'markdown' or 'text'

    Returns dict with:
        'document': the formatted SOO text/markdown
        'summary': section count, output count, PID count, timer count
        'confidence_note': description confidence breakdown

tools.name: generate_network_topology
tools.description:
Generate a Graphviz DOT diagram of the complete plant network
    topology showing all PLC-to-PLC communication paths, HMI
    connections, and Ignition SCADA links.

    The DOT output can be rendered with Graphviz, pasted into
    an online viewer (https://dreampuf.github.io/GraphvizOnline/),
    or saved as a .dot file.

    Args:
        include_hmi: include FTView HMI connections (default True)
        include_ignition: include Ignition OPC-UA device connections (default True)
        highlight_plc: optional PLC ID to highlight in the diagram

    Returns:
        'dot': the complete DOT string
        'stats': dict with plc_count, msg_links, produced_consumed,
                 hmi_connections, ignition_devices
        'render_hint': instructions for rendering the diagram

tools.name: generate_plc_impact_diagram
tools.description:
Generate a Graphviz DOT diagram showing one PLC and everything
    connected to it — the visual version of plc_impact_analysis.

    Shows: upstream/downstream MSG links, produced/consumed tags,
    HMI screens, Ignition devices, all centered on the target PLC.

    Args:
        plc_id: PLC identifier (e.g., 'CH530001')

    Returns:
        'dot': the DOT string
        'stats': dict with upstream, downstream, hmi_screens, ignition_devices
        'render_hint': instructions for rendering

tools.name: generate_logic_flow
tools.description:
Generate a Graphviz DOT diagram showing signal/logic flow within a PLC.

    Four effective modes:
    - address + mode='data':  trace MOV/COP/ADD data flow (original behavior)
    - address + mode='logic': trace XIC/XIO backward logic flow (new)
    - routine provided:       show all signal flow in that routine
    - neither:                show top-level program structure with JSR call graph

    The mode parameter applies only when address is provided. Default 'data'
    preserves full backward compatibility.

    Args:
        plc_id:     PLC identifier (e.g., 'CH880001')
        address:    Optional address to trace (e.g., 'O:125/2', 'PD10:0').
                    Accepts PLC-5 shorthand (B13/913) or canonical (B13:57/1).
        routine:    Optional routine to visualize (e.g., 'MainRoutine')
        max_depth:  Max levels of signal/contact following (default 5)
        mode:       'data' (default) traces MOV/COP data flow.
                    'logic' traces XIC/XIO backward contact logic via
                    trace_logic_chain. Only applies when address is provided.

    Returns:
        'dot': Graphviz DOT string
        'mode': 'logic_trace', 'signal_trace', 'routine_flow', or
                'program_structure'
        'stats': dict with node/edge counts (logic mode adds
                 rungs_examined, terminals_found, max_depth_hit)
        'render_hint': how to render the diagram
        'summary': plain-English narrative (logic mode only)

tools.name: generate_subsystem_diagram
tools.description:
Generate a Graphviz DOT diagram for a specific subsystem
    defined by a list of key addresses.

    Use this to visualize a control loop, equipment module, or
    any functional grouping of signals within a PLC.

    Example: generate_subsystem_diagram('CH880001',
        ['N12:564', 'PD10:30', 'N12:400'])
    Produces a visual diagram of the PM Office HVAC control loop.

    Args:
        plc_id: PLC identifier
        addresses: list of key addresses defining the subsystem

    Returns:
        'dot': the DOT string
        'stats': dict with primary_addresses, total_nodes, total_edges, rungs_covered
        'render_hint': how to render the diagram

tools.name: full_plc_documentation
tools.description:
Run the complete 19-step documentation pipeline for a PLC.

    Generates all analysis documents, Graphviz diagrams, and a knowledge
    graph. Stores everything in the NEXUS database for future retrieval.

    This is the single-command full documentation workflow. Run it once per
    PLC. Re-run to update (versions are tracked; old versions are superseded
    but preserved).

    Args:
        plc_id: PLC identifier (e.g., 'CH880001')

    Returns:
        Pipeline result with step log, artifact counts, and timing.

tools.name: get_plc_document
tools.description:
Retrieve a stored document for a PLC.

    Doc types: program_structure, io_map, pid_analysis, anomaly_report,
    migration_assessment, sequence_of_operations, master_index

    Returns the current (non-superseded) version.

tools.name: get_plc_diagram
tools.description:
Retrieve a stored diagram (Graphviz DOT) for a PLC.

    Diagram types: network_impact, network_full, program_structure,
    logic_flow_[subsystem], mind_map

    Returns the DOT string ready for rendering.

tools.name: get_plc_knowledge_graph
tools.description:
Retrieve the knowledge graph for a PLC.

    Optionally filter by node_type: controller, program, routine,
    input, output, pid_loop, hmi_screen

    Returns nodes and edges for rendering or analysis.

tools.name: find_docs_for_tag
tools.description:
Vault notes that reference a NEXUS tag (confirmed + inferred), confirmed first.

    Returns a list of dicts with keys:
        file_path, plc_id, title, domain, ref_type
    Returns [] if no vault notes reference the tag.

tools.name: get_vault_note
tools.description:
Frontmatter + body of a vault note, given its path relative to the vault root.

    Reads the .md from disk (the index does not store body text). Returns
    {"file_path","plc_id","title","domain","frontmatter","body","wikilinks",
     "confirmed_tags","inferred_tags","last_scanned"}.

    Rejects path traversal: resolves the path against the vault root and
    verifies the resolved path stays inside it.  Returns {"error": ...} for
    traversal attempts, missing files, and unexpected read failures.

tools.name: generate_dox_tree
tools.description:
Generate a DOX AGENTS.md hierarchy for a PLC in the active NEXUS DB.

    Writes a regenerable, never-hand-edited tree to:
      <NEXUS_SOURCE_ROOT>/.nexus/dox/<client_code>/<plc_id>/  (plant PLCs)
      <NEXUS_LIBRARY_ROOT>/.nexus/dox/<client_code>/<plc_id>/ (library PLCs)

    Plant/library routing is derived from the plcs.is_library flag set at ingest.
    Client code is derived from the PLC ID prefix (CH###### → CTD, NFK-…→NFK, etc.).

    Emits:
    - .nexus/dox/AGENTS.md                             build-artifact warning (once per root)
    - <client>/<plc_id>/AGENTS.md                      PLC summary + child index
    - <client>/<plc_id>/areas/<ordinal>-<slug>/AGENTS.md  area derivation, FND, ANM, routing

    Inline (stamped, DB-sourced): confirmed findings (FND) + ANM counts.
    Routed (live, tool-computed): address_xref, find_interlocks, coverage_gap.

    The tool performs NO DB writes and NO processor communication.
    Atomic swap: rename(live→bak) → rename(tmp→live) → rmtree(bak).
    Leftover detection on entry handles crashes mid-swap.

    Args:
        plc_id: PLC identifier (e.g. 'CH880001').

    Returns a dict with:
        generated_root, files, area_count, findings_counts, anomaly_counts, freshness.
